name: P = NP

phase_0.boundary_condition: The Frobenius identity μ∘δ = id as the closure condition on the complexity problem

VINIT.justification: The void state before any distinction between P and NP is made; the pre-computational state of pure possibility.

TANCH.justification: The terminal anchor that closes the system: the condition that the round-trip through differentiation and reintegration returns the original problem without loss.

AFWD.chosen_element: Polynomial-time reduction (e.g., SAT to any NP problem)
AFWD.justification: The forward morphism that maps between problems, preserving their structural relationships in the complexity hierarchy.

AREV.justification: The reverse morphism that seeks to separate the classes, the descent into the space of lower bounds and barriers.

CLINK.justification: The composition of morphisms that links the entire web of NP-complete problems, forming the categorical backbone of the theory.

IMSCRIB.justification: The identity element: the problem's capacity to refer to itself, the Gödelian core that generates the undecidable.

FSPLIT.chosen_element: The complexity class question (P vs NP)
FSPLIT.justification: Splits into two distinct branches: the affirmative (P=NP) and the negative (P≠NP) possibilities.

FFUSE.chosen_element: The structural equivalence under the Frobenius identity
FFUSE.justification: Reconstitutes the original problem from the two branches; the condition that the round-trip through the split preserves the problem's identity.

EVALT.justification: The affirmative evaluation: the existence of polynomial-time algorithms for all NP problems.

EVALF.justification: The negative evaluation: the proven separation of complexity classes.

ENGAGR.chosen_element: The paraconsistent state where both P=NP and P≠NP are held
ENGAGR.justification: A paradice: both possibilities simultaneously maintained in the Belnap-Dunn four-valued logic until resolution.

IFIX.chosen_element: The permanent record of a proof or disproof (e.g., the Lean formalization)
IFIX.justification: The irreversible fixation of the solution into the formal system, the append-only record of computational truth.

phase_2.split_element: The complexity class question (P vs NP)
phase_2.split_input: The undifferentiated problem of whether P equals NP
phase_2.fuse_element: The structural equivalence under the Frobenius identity
phase_2.fuse_result: The original problem statement, now understood as a fixed point of the split-and-fuse cycle

phase_3.void_description: The pre-computational state where no distinction between polynomial and nondeterministic polynomial time exists; the void of unclassified problems.
phase_3.true_description: The state where P=NP is proven: every problem in NP has a polynomial-time solution, collapsing the complexity hierarchy.
phase_3.false_description: The state where P≠NP is proven: there exist problems in NP that cannot be solved in polynomial time, establishing a permanent separation.
phase_3.both_description: The paraconsistent state where both P=NP and P≠NP are admissible truth values, the B-state of the Belnap lattice until a proof is found.

steps.domain_action: The void of unclassified computational problems
The Frobenius identity μ∘δ = id as the closure condition
Polynomial-time reduction from SAT to any NP problem
The search for lower bounds and barriers to P=NP
The chain of reductions linking NP-complete problems
The complexity class question splits into two branches
The P=NP branch is entered and explored
Within P=NP, the forward direction of polynomial-time algorithms
The P≠NP branch is entered and explored
Within P≠NP, the reverse direction of lower bounds
The two branches are fused back via the Frobenius identity
The system enters the paraconsistent B-state, holding both possibilities
A proof or disproof is permanently recorded in the formal system

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The IMASM compiler that translates the complexity problem into a sequence of categorical operations
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The communication between the P=NP and P≠NP branches via polynomial reductions and barrier arguments
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The Lean 4 proof assistant kernel that stores the formal verification of theorems and the paraconsistent flag
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The order of exploration: first split, then investigate each branch, then attempt fusion, and finally record the result
phase_5.alfs_store: The Lean 4 library with the paraconsistent kernel fork, serving as the canonical reference for formal verification

phase_6.cycle_cost: Information processed per reduction or proof step
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: The unresolved problem, with both P=NP and P≠NP as possibilities
phase_6.post_cycle_state: The resolved problem, with one branch validated or the system stabilized in the B-state
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The Frobenius identity ensures the round-trip through split and fuse is lossless; no information is erased in the structural cycle
